| Category = Vegetarian recipes
| Servings = 6–8
| Energy = 320 Kcal per burger
| Time = 20 minutes
| Rating = 2
}}{{recipe}}

This recipe for '''beanburgers''' has been adapted from a Somerfield recipe as part of a Food Technology GCSE course in the UK. By "adapted", I mean "changed almost unrecognisably". The original is [http://www.somerfield.co.uk/foodanddrink/recipes/recipesearch/recipe.asp?recipe=Beany+Burgers+%26+Tomato+Salsa here]: you can see for yourself.

These beanburgers work best in [[Cookbook:Pita|pita breads]] (crisped up in the oven), with tomato and lettuce. Alternatively, they taste nice with a spicy tomato sauce.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 red or yellow [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], chopped
* 1 generous [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] each of [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:Coriander|ground coriander]], [[Cookbook:Chilli Powder|mild chilli powder]], [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]] and [[Cookbook:turmeric|turmeric]]
* 2 tins of mixed [[cookbook:beans|beans]], drained
* 2–3 medium [[Cookbook:carrot|carrot]]s, [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]]
* 40 g [[Cookbook:Rolled oats|rolled oats]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]]

== Procedure ==
# [[cookbook:Fry|Fry]] the onions and pepper (in a little bit of oil) with the spices for a couple of minutes. Leave to cool.
# Mash the beans in a large bowl.
# Add the carrot, onion, pepper and oats to the mashed beans and mix until well combined.
# Add the egg gradually (you probably won't need all of it). You don't want a mixture that's too sticky.
# Shape the dough into 6 to 8 burgers and lightly flour each side.
# Fry the burgers (in a little bit of oil) for a few minutes on each side, until golden.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can leave out the egg to make it vegan. However, without it, the burger breaks and frays much more in the pan.
